outputs.L1:
The present invention provides, in an economical manner, a method and device for producing a high-viscosity polylactic acid foam-molding material suitable for foam molding at a high expansion ratio, as well as a foam-molded article having a high expansion ratio and formed from said polylactic acid composition.

A polylactic acid foam-molding material having an MI value of 0.05–5, measured in accordance with JIS K7210 at 190°C under a 21.6-kg load, is produced by physically or mechanically reducing the molecular weight and rebonding, in the presence of a supercritical inert gas, polylactic acid having a polystyrene-equivalent molecular weight of 2,000,000 or higher as measured by GPC. This polylactic acid is generated when three types of crosslinked polylactic acid (A), (B), and (C), having different component ratios of D and L isomers and obtained by reacting polylactic acid composed of D and L isomers with a crosslinking agent, are mixed at a weight ratio of 25–50:25–50:25–50, wherein (A)+(B)+(C)=100, and the resulting mixture is melted.

A foam-molded article is produced by providing a grinding orifice on an injection-molding machine or an extrusion-molding machine, discharging the material from a die at a temperature ranging from the softening point to 110°C, and subjecting the discharged material to foam molding.
outputs.L2:
The invention offers, in an economical manner, a process and apparatus for manufacturing a high-viscosity polylactic acid material for foam molding that is appropriate for high-expansion-ratio foaming, as well as a highly expanded foam molded product made from that polylactic acid composition.

The polylactic acid foam molding material has an MI value of 0.05 to 5, as determined according to JIS K7210 at 190°C under a load of 21.6 kg. This material is obtained by using polylactic acid having, by GPC measurement, a polystyrene-equivalent molecular weight of at least 2,000,000, which is produced when three crosslinked polylactic acids (A), (B), and (C), each having different D-isomer and L-isomer component ratios and each prepared by reacting a polylactic acid composed of D and L isomers with a crosslinking agent, are blended at a weight ratio of 25–50:25–50:25–50, provided that (A) + (B) + (C) = 100, and the resulting blend is melted. In the presence of a supercritical inert gas, the molecular weight is then reduced physically or mechanically and subsequently recombined to form the foam molding material.

A foam molded article is produced by equipping an injection molding machine or extrusion molding machine with a grinding orifice, extruding the material from a die at a temperature ranging from the softening point to 110°C, and carrying out foam molding.
outputs.L3:
The invention provides an economical method and device for producing a high-viscosity polylactic acid foam molding material that is suitable for high-expansion foam molding. The material can be used to obtain foam molded articles having a high expansion ratio while maintaining desirable moldability and mechanical properties.

The polylactic acid foam molding material produced by this method has a melt index (MI) value in the range of 0.05 to 5. The MI value is measured in accordance with JIS K7210 at a temperature of 190°C under a load of 21.6 kg. By controlling the MI value within this range, the material achieves the viscosity required for stable foam molding, particularly for forming highly expanded molded articles.

The material is produced by reducing the molecular weight of a high-molecular-weight polylactic acid and then rebonding the polymer chains in the presence of a supercritical inert gas. This treatment makes it possible to obtain a polylactic acid material having an appropriate viscosity and melt strength for foam molding. The use of a supercritical inert gas also contributes to efficient processing and improved foamability.

The high-molecular-weight polylactic acid used as the starting material is generated by mixing and melting three types of crosslinked polylactic acids having different D-isomer and L-isomer ratios. These three crosslinked polylactic acids are blended in specified weight proportions and then melted together to form the high-molecular-weight polylactic acid. By adjusting the isomer ratios and the blending proportions, the crystallinity, melt behavior, and foam-molding characteristics of the resulting material can be controlled.

A high-expansion foam molded article is produced from the polylactic acid foam molding material using an injection molding machine or an extrusion molding machine provided with a grinding orifice. During molding, the material is discharged from a die at a temperature within the range from the softening point of the material to 110°C. This temperature control enables stable expansion of the material and allows the formation of a high-expansion foam molded article with good shape retention.

Thus, the invention enables the economical production of a high-viscosity polylactic acid foam molding material and provides a practical method for manufacturing high-expansion polylactic acid foam molded articles using conventional molding equipment adapted with a grinding orifice.
outputs.L4:
The present invention relates to a polylactic acid foam molding material and to a method for producing a high-expansion polylactic acid foam molded article using the material. More particularly, the invention provides an economical technique for preparing a high-viscosity polylactic acid resin composition suitable for foam molding, especially for producing lightweight molded articles having a high expansion ratio.

Polylactic acid is a biodegradable and plant-derived resin and is therefore attractive as an environmentally friendly alternative to petroleum-based plastics. However, ordinary polylactic acid generally has insufficient melt strength for high-expansion foaming. When conventional polylactic acid is subjected to injection foaming or extrusion foaming, the cell structure tends to collapse, the expansion ratio is limited, and stable molding is difficult. In order to obtain a high-expansion foam, it is necessary to increase the melt viscosity and melt tension of the resin while maintaining processability. Existing methods for achieving this often require complicated reactions, expensive modifiers, or difficult processing conditions, making practical large-scale production uneconomical.

The invention solves these problems by preparing a foam molding material from a mixture of three types of crosslinked polylactic acids having different D/L isomer ratios. By combining polylactic acids that differ in stereochemical composition, the crystallization behavior, melt viscosity, and foaming characteristics of the resin can be adjusted. The use of crosslinked polylactic acids further improves melt strength and allows the resin to retain gas during foaming, thereby enabling the production of molded articles with a high expansion ratio.

In the production method, the three crosslinked polylactic acids are mixed and processed in the presence of a supercritical inert gas. During this treatment, the molecular weight of the polylactic acid is temporarily reduced and then rebonded or reconstructed under controlled conditions. This molecular weight adjustment improves the uniformity and flow characteristics of the resin while maintaining the high viscosity required for foam molding. The supercritical inert gas acts as a processing medium and foaming aid, promoting uniform dispersion and enabling stable molding without excessive thermal degradation of the polylactic acid.

The resin composition obtained by this method has a melt index, or MI value, in the range of 0.05 to 5. This MI range indicates that the material has sufficiently high viscosity and melt strength for high-expansion foam molding while still being capable of being discharged from molding equipment. If the MI value is too high, the resin becomes too fluid and cannot maintain a stable foamed structure. If the MI value is too low, discharge and molding become difficult. Therefore, the specified MI range is important for balancing moldability and foamability.

The prepared polylactic acid foam molding material can be molded by an injection molding process or an extrusion molding process. In either process, the material is discharged through a grinding orifice or similar discharge portion, which applies mechanical shearing and pressure control to the molten resin. This contributes to uniform cell formation and stable expansion of the resin as it exits the molding equipment. By controlling the discharge temperature and foaming temperature, the resin can be expanded in a stable manner to form a high-expansion polylactic acid foam molded article.

The resulting molded article is lightweight, has a high expansion ratio, and is composed mainly of polylactic acid. Because the material has improved melt strength and controlled crystallization behavior, the foam cells can be maintained without severe collapse or shrinkage. The invention therefore makes it possible to manufacture practical polylactic acid foam products that were previously difficult to produce using ordinary PLA resin.

The invention is useful for producing a wide range of molded foam articles, including cushioning materials, packaging materials, containers, trays, heat-insulating articles, structural lightweight components, and other biodegradable or environmentally compatible plastic products. Since the method enables economical production using polylactic acid as the principal resin, it provides a practical industrial route for manufacturing high-expansion PLA foams with reduced environmental impact.
outputs.L5:
The JIS and GPC systems play important roles in organizing, standardizing, and identifying products and information across industries. The JIS, or Japanese Industrial Standards, provide guidelines that help ensure quality, safety, and consistency in manufacturing and technical processes. These standards are widely used in Japan and are recognized internationally in many sectors.

GPC, or Global Product Classification, is another important system used to categorize products in a structured and consistent way. It helps businesses, suppliers, and retailers communicate clearly about goods in global supply chains. By using GPC, companies can improve product data accuracy, reduce confusion, and make trade more efficient.

The connection between JIS and GPC highlights the value of standardization in modern business. While JIS focuses on technical and industrial standards, GPC supports product classification and identification. Together, they help create a more organized, reliable, and transparent marketplace.

counterfactuals.prompt: Write a patent-style abstract describing an invention for producing high-viscosity polylactic acid foam molding material using crosslinked PLA isomer mixtures, supercritical inert gas, and extrusion or injection foam molding.
counterfactuals.output: A method is disclosed for producing a high-viscosity polylactic acid (PLA) foam molding material and molded foam article. The method comprises blending stereochemically different PLA resins, including poly(L-lactic acid), poly(D-lactic acid), and/or copolymers thereof, to form a PLA isomer mixture capable of stereocomplex formation, introducing a multifunctional chain-extending or crosslinking agent to increase melt strength, and melt-kneading the mixture under conditions sufficient to form a partially crosslinked high-viscosity PLA composition. A supercritical inert gas, such as carbon dioxide or nitrogen, is injected into the molten composition under pressure to form a single-phase polymer/gas solution. The solution is subsequently expanded through extrusion foaming or injection foam molding to produce a cellular PLA molding material having improved foamability, dimensional stability, heat resistance, and mechanical strength. The crosslinked PLA isomer mixture provides enhanced melt elasticity and gas retention, enabling formation of fine and uniform cells at relatively high expansion ratios while maintaining biodegradability and suitability for packaging, cushioning, automotive, and structural molded applications.
counterfactuals.label: cf_1

counterfactuals.prompt: Generate a single-paragraph technical patent summary for a PLA foam molding material with MI 0.05–5 measured by JIS K7210 at 190°C/21.6 kg, made from three crosslinked D/L polylactic acid compositions and used to form high-expansion foam articles.
counterfactuals.output: A polylactic acid (PLA) foam molding material is provided for producing high-expansion foam molded articles, the material having a melt index (MI) of 0.05 to 5 g/10 min as measured in accordance with JIS K7210 at 190°C under a 21.6 kg load, and comprising a blend of three crosslinked polylactic acid compositions differing in D/L-lactic acid unit configuration and/or stereochemical composition, each composition being crosslinked to impart enhanced melt strength and foaming stability. By combining the three crosslinked D/L-polylactic acid compositions in controlled proportions, the molding material exhibits improved strain hardening behavior, reduced melt flow, and sufficient viscoelasticity to retain gas during expansion, thereby enabling formation of uniform, closed-cell, high-expansion PLA foam articles. The material is suitable for extrusion foaming, bead foaming, foam sheet production, and molded foam articles requiring biodegradability, heat resistance, dimensional stability, lightweight structure, and improved mechanical properties relative to conventional non-crosslinked PLA foams.
counterfactuals.label: cf_2

counterfactuals.prompt: Draft an English patent abstract for a method and device that economically produce high-expansion polylactic acid foam by mixing three crosslinked PLA types, lowering and rebonding molecular weight in supercritical gas, and molding through a die.
counterfactuals.output: A method and apparatus for economically producing high-expansion polylactic acid foam are disclosed. The method includes blending three types of crosslinked polylactic acid resins having different crosslinking structures or molecular characteristics to form a polylactic acid composition, introducing the composition into an extruder, and supplying a supercritical gas to the molten composition. Under controlled temperature, pressure, and shear conditions, the molecular weight of the polylactic acid is temporarily reduced to improve melt flow and gas impregnation, and is subsequently recombined or rebonded to restore melt strength suitable for foaming. The resulting gas-containing melt is extruded through a molding die, where pressure release causes expansion and formation of a uniform high-expansion foam. The apparatus includes a raw-material mixing unit, an extrusion plasticizing unit, a supercritical gas injection unit, a molecular-weight control section configured to promote molecular scission and rebonding, and a die for shaping and foaming the composition. The invention enables stable continuous manufacture of lightweight, biodegradable polylactic acid foam with improved expansion ratio, cell uniformity, and production economy.
counterfactuals.label: cf_3

counterfactuals.prompt: Create an invention disclosure paragraph about manufacturing high-viscosity PLA foam molding resin from crosslinked polylactic acid components A, B, and C in ratios totaling 100, then foaming it with an injection or extrusion molding machine equipped with a grinding orifice.
counterfactuals.output: Disclosed is a method for manufacturing a high-viscosity polylactic acid (PLA) foam molding resin and molded foam articles therefrom. The method comprises preparing a crosslinked PLA resin composition by combining crosslinked polylactic acid components A, B, and C in predetermined weight ratios, wherein the sum of A+B+C is 100 parts by weight. Component A may comprise a high-molecular-weight or highly branched crosslinked PLA fraction providing melt strength, component B may comprise a lower-viscosity crosslinked PLA fraction providing processability and flow control, and component C may comprise a functionalized or chain-extended crosslinked PLA fraction configured to enhance cell formation, thermal resistance, and dimensional stability during foaming. The blended resin composition is melt-kneaded to form a uniform high-viscosity PLA foam molding resin having increased melt elasticity suitable for retaining gas during expansion. The resin is then supplied to an injection molding machine or extrusion molding machine equipped with a grinding orifice, through which the molten resin is subjected to controlled shear, pressure drop, and dispersion to improve homogenization of the crosslinked PLA phase and promote uniform foaming. A physical or chemical blowing agent may be introduced before or during molding, and the resin is foamed and shaped in a mold or die to produce a biodegradable PLA foam article having fine, stable cells, improved mechanical strength, and reduced density.
counterfactuals.label: cf_4

counterfactuals.prompt: Translate into patent-abstract style a Japanese technical description of producing a polylactic acid foam molded article having high expansion ratio, including GPC molecular weight of 2,000,000+, MI value range, supercritical inert gas treatment, and die discharge temperature from softening point to 110°C.
counterfactuals.output: A polylactic acid foam molded article having a high expansion ratio is produced by using, as a raw material, a polylactic acid resin having a weight-average molecular weight of not less than 2,000,000 as measured by GPC and a melt index within a predetermined range suitable for foam molding. The polylactic acid resin is impregnated with an inert gas in a supercritical state, and the resulting gas-containing resin is discharged through a die while controlling the resin temperature at the die outlet to a temperature from the softening point of the resin to 110°C. By controlling the molecular weight, melt flow characteristics, supercritical inert gas impregnation conditions, and die discharge temperature, a polylactic acid foam molded article having uniform cells and an excellent high expansion ratio can be obtained.
counterfactuals.label: cf_5
